items.definition: A setting that stops the machine starting until you hold the lock button for a few seconds.
items.example: Hold the padlock button for three seconds to release the child lock.

items.definition: An unplanned stop in which the car cannot be driven safely. It is the stop, not the specific fault that caused it.
items.example: I have had a breakdown on the motorway, and I need a recovery vehicle.

items.definition: The service that comes to help a broken-down car. It comes through insurance, a manufacturer package or a separate membership.
items.example: Do you know whether my roadside assistance covers a call-out in this area?

items.definition: The van or truck sent to collect the car. Some can lift a car and some can only tow it on a wheel.
items.example: The recovery vehicle will lift the car, so I do not need to empty the boot.

items.definition: All four indicators blink together. The car is stationary or unusual. Severity level 1 — Information / Status. Action: Nothing to do while the lights are on. Switch them off once the car moves again..
The red reflective triangle placed on the road behind a stopped vehicle so drivers see it in time.
items.example: Put the warning triangle out about 100 metres behind the car.

items.definition: Starting a car with a flat battery by connecting it to the battery of another car with cables.
items.example: Could you send someone to jump start the car? The battery is flat.

items.definition: A unit of energy in food. One gram of fat holds about 9 kcal, a gram of carbohydrate or protein about 4.
items.example: This bar contains 250 kcal, which is about a tenth of a day's energy.

items.definition: The date after which the food is still safe to eat but has gone down in quality. A quality date, not a safety date.
items.example: The best-before date has passed, so the biscuits are only stale, not bad.

items.definition: The date after which the food may no longer be safe to eat. It is a safety date and it is not negotiable.
items.example: The use-by date was yesterday, so I threw the chicken away.

items.definition: The amount of the product the nutrition figures are given for. It is the maker's choice, so it often does not match what you eat.
items.example: One serving is 30 g, which is much less than the bowl I had.

items.definition: A substance in food that can cause a serious allergic reaction in some people. There are fourteen that have to be declared.
items.example: The allergen box says it contains peanuts and soya.

items.definition: The unbroken path a chilled product follows from the factory to your fridge. If the chain breaks, the use-by date stops meaning anything.
items.example: The cold chain was broken, so the date on the pack means nothing.

items.definition: To put something that has thawed back into the freezer. For meat and fish this is a safety question, not a quality one.
items.example: You can freeze it now, but you cannot refreeze it once it has thawed.

items.definition: The flow of electricity, measured in amperes (A).
items.example: The current went back through the earth conductor instead of through the motor.

items.definition: A machine that moves water from one place to another.
items.example: The pump in the sump moves the water up into the tank.

items.definition: A pump whose motor is sealed in a case that works under water.
items.example: A submersible pump hangs on a cable inside the well.

items.definition: The material around the live part of a cable that keeps the current inside it.
items.example: The insulation on the cable is cracked where it passes over the edge of the pit.

items.definition: Current that escapes from the live part of a cable or a pump through damaged insulation.
items.example: The electrician measured the leakage current before he ran the pump again.

items.definition: A deep hole dug in the ground that holds the water a pump lifts.
items.example: The pump hangs ten metres down inside the well.

items.definition: A pit that collects water from a floor or a basement so that a pump can lift it.
items.example: The sump in the basement pit fills when the floor drain backs up.

items.definition: The green-and-yellow wire that connects the metal parts of an installation to the earth.
items.example: The earth conductor was cut by a drill during the renovation.

items.definition: The whole arrangement that connects the metal parts of an installation to the earth, so that a fault current has a safe way back.
items.example: The earthing of the pump was checked when the board was replaced.

items.definition: A device that compares the current going out with the current coming back, and opens the circuit when they differ.
items.example: The residual-current device is the wide switch on the board with the test button.

items.definition: The IP code on the nameplate that says how well the casing keeps out solid objects and water.
items.example: The nameplate of this pump carries an ingress protection rating of IP68.

items.definition: A switch on a float that starts or stops the pump when the water level rises or falls.
items.example: The float switch in the tank stops the pump when the tank is empty.

items.definition: The pump turning without water around it, so that the motor has nothing to cool it.
items.example: A dry run heats the motor of a submersible pump.

items.definition: Water moving in the wrong direction, back along the pipe towards the pump.
items.example: After the supply stops, backflow can leave the pump running with no water.

items.definition: The push of electric charge that drives a current.
items.example: The voltage across the cell is 12 V.

items.definition: The green-and-yellow conductor that ties the metal case of an appliance to the earth bar in the board.
items.example: The earth wire was cut by a drill during the last renovation.

items.definition: A device that opens a circuit when the current is higher than the circuit is rated for.
items.example: The circuit breaker is the 16 A device on the board.

items.definition: Joining metal parts to each other so that they cannot sit at different voltages.
items.example: Bonding of the metal pipework is part of the installation.

items.definition: To open the circuit by itself, because the device has found a fault or an overload.
items.example: The RCD tripped when the heater was switched on.

items.definition: A valve on the tank that opens and releases water if the pressure or the temperature inside becomes too high.
items.example: The safety valve is the small brass valve on the cold pipe.

items.definition: A rod of metal that corrodes instead of the tank, so that the tank wall is saved.
items.example: The anode rod is checked at every service and replaced when it is worn away.

items.definition: A burn caused by hot liquid or steam.
items.example: Water at 60 °C can scald a child in a few seconds.

items.definition: Removing the mineral scale that builds up inside a tank and on the heating element.
items.example: Descaling is done at the service interval in hard water areas.

items.definition: An animal that lived a very long time ago, long before people. Dinosaurs are gone now, but their bones turn to stone under the ground.
items.example: The long-necked dinosaur pulled leaves from the treetop.

items.definition: The hard part of an animal that turned to stone after a very long time. Fossils tell us what the animal looked like.
items.example: She found a yellow fossil under a huge leaf.

items.definition: The mark a foot leaves in soft ground. Big animals leave big footprints, and they show which way the animal walked.
items.example: The footprints pointed deeper into the valley.
